newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee closes at 35.62/63 against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee closes at 35.62/63 against dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.62/63 per dollar on Thursday after opening the day at 35.65/66, dealers said.
The rupee began gaining in early morning session on dollar selling pressure by a major bank, dealers said. The dollar recovered later after the same bank started buying, they said.
"Maybe there was corporate demand (in the morning session)," said a dealer at a state-run bank, saying it was rather unusual for the same bank to be buying dollars on the same day.
"Or may be it was a strategy. We don't know," he said.
The rupee touched a high of 35.59 on Thursday.
The Reserve Bank of India made enquiries but did not intervene, dealers at major banks said.
Forward premia on dollars fell sharply on reports of an impending cut in cash reserve requirements for Indian banks. The premia recovered slightly towards the close.
An October 2 report on global economics and currencies by Merrill Lynch said the rupee was expected to remain stable at 35-36 per dollar in the near term.
It expected a 4.0 percent depreciation in the rupee's value in 1997 to make up for the inflation differential between India and its major trading partners.
